audit_findings.title: Opioid settlement may be omitted or counted repeatedly
audit_findings.magnitude: $773.8 million accrued ($599.8 million net of tax), equal to 10.7% of $7,215 million base equity value; $136.6 million of settlement cash is included within current cash
audit_findings.mechanism: The settlement must enter either as a one-time reduction through OE or as a present-value liability deduction from the equity bridge, but must not be omitted or propagated through the recurring OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: These related payments are expected to be made over a period of nine years , with slightly more than one-third of the total amount payable within the first two years and the remainder payable over the following seven years .
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and charge are demonstrated, but their treatment in the $491.6 million anchor is unresolved. Stripping the charge without deducting the liability overstates value; growing an anchor depressed by the one-time charge understates value by repeating it indefinitely. Either treatment is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $773.8 million charge through the FY2026 OE workpapers and the $307.9 million cash/STI bridge; then rerun with normalized OE and exactly one after-tax present-value settlement deduction.

audit_findings.title: Current shares may be paired with stale interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: Q1 interest of $166.7 million annualizes to $541.8 million versus $504.2 million in FY2025, a computed $37.6 million pre-tax or approximately $28.0 million after tax using the filed 25.5% Q1 rate; indicated base-value effect approximately $0.79 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A full-year interest normalization reduces equity-level OE associated with the latest debt-funded repurchases while the reduced share count remains in the denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The ASR Agreement was funded with $ 750.0 million of borrowings under the ABL Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: FY interest reflects only part of the period after the debt-funded repurchases, while the valuation uses approximately current shares. The filed quarterly run rate indicates a base value near $13.73 rather than $14.52, still above the $12.55 price, while the corresponding buy-below level remains below the price. On the supplied scale, it does not independently change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-year interest schedule from the June 2026 debt balances and contractual rates, replace partial-period interest in anchor OE, and rerun using the same 496.826 million shares.

audit_findings.title: Additional opioid exposure remains outside the settlement
audit_findings.mechanism: Any Washington judgment or settlement would reduce OE if expensed or require an after-tax present-value liability deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Opioid Settlement Framework does not include the State of Washington.
audit_findings.explanation: The excluded Washington claim and ongoing trial are demonstrated, but the company could not determine the outcome probability or reasonably possible loss range and recorded no separately quantified allowance. The exposure may affect value, but the supplied record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Washington trial outcome, any subsequent reserve or disclosed loss range, and insurance or tax-recovery evidence; rerun the bridge when a supportable after-tax cash claim can be quantified.

audit_findings.title: Pension accounting income may exceed cash economics
audit_findings.magnitude: Potential FY2025 adjustment of $85.3 million, comprising $28.4 million of pension and post-retirement income plus $56.9 million of cash contributions; computed base-value sensitivity approximately $2.41 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: OE should remove non-service pension accounting income and deduct sponsored-plan cash contributions not otherwise captured as operating expense or maintenance capex.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to contribute approximately $ 50 million to its pension and post-retirement plans in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting income and cash contributions are filed amounts, but their treatment in OE is unresolved. If neither adjustment was made, the $85.3 million difference equals 17.4% of the $491.6 million anchor and would reduce computed base value from $14.52 to about $12.11, below the $12.55 market price. This is capable of reversing the base-case conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to the cash-flow pension lines, remove the $28.4 million accounting income, deduct the $56.9 million sponsored-plan contributions, exclude already-expensed multiemployer contributions, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease reinvestment can bypass cash capex
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease additions were $45.3 million and finance-lease amortization was $40.6 million; charging the entire $45.3 million would reduce computed base value by approximately $1.28 per share to $13.24
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease amortization is added back in OE, the maintenance portion of noncash finance-lease asset additions must enter maintenance reinvestment even though it appears outside cash investing outflows.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance leases are included in Property and equipment, net, current maturities of long-term debt and finance lease obligations and long-term debt and finance lease obligations on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The lease amounts are demonstrated, but inclusion in eligible D&A and the maintenance share of additions remain unresolved. Even the conservative assumption that all $45.3 million of additions was omitted maintenance reinvestment leaves base value above the $12.55 price and leaves the price above the reduced buy-below threshold, so the supplied maximum does not independently change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify finance-lease amortization within eligible D&A, classify the $45.3 million of additions between maintenance and growth, and rerun OE with the supported maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains a 53rd week
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed incremental effect was $68 million of Adjusted EBITDA and $0.03 per adjusted share, approximately $16.7 million using 555.4 million adjusted diluted shares; the latter is 3.4% of anchor OE and implies approximately $0.47 per share of base-value sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: The extra week's after-tax OE contribution must be removed from the anchor before applying annual growth and terminal-value assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal 2025 includes an estimated $68 million of incremental Adjusted EBITDA due to the impact of the additional 53rd week.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53rd week is demonstrated, but Adjusted EBITDA is not an OE adjustment. The filed adjusted-net-income effect provides the closest after-tax scale: removing approximately $16.7 million would lower base value from $14.52 to about $14.05, still above the $12.55 price, and would leave the price above the approximately $9.84 recomputed buy-below level. It does not change the conclusion on the available scale.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the extra week's actual net income, eligible D&A and maintenance reinvestment, remove the resulting after-tax OE contribution, and confirm the scenario rerun remains within the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 residual D&A of $289.8 million, equal to 15.9% of filed D&A and 58.9% of the $491.6 million anchor; full eligibility would increase computed base value by approximately $8.20 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A shown by filed evidence to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE, increasing the anchor and all scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $36.9m (2.1% of filed D&A); FY2021 $183.4m (11.9% of filed D&A); FY2022 $240.8m (14.3% of filed D&A); FY2025 $289.8m (15.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving the residual as an expense is conservative and cannot overstate value. Eligibility is unresolved rather than demonstrated, but the classified pool is sufficiently large that a supportable portion could materially raise intrinsic value and potentially lift the margin-of-safety threshold above the market price.
audit_findings.action: Map the $289.8 million residual to fixed-asset depreciation, finance-lease amortization, acquired-intangible amortization, software amortization and other components; add back only filed-supported eligible amounts and rerun all scenarios.
